section: Vice-President; Prime Minister and the Union Council of Ministers - Articles 74, 75, 77, 78
subsections: Council of Ministers - collective and individual responsibility
Prime Minister - appointment, qualifications, oath, real executive

accepted.s: Under Article 75(5) of the Constitution of India, a person appointed as a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament must become a member within
accepted.x: Article 75(5) requires a non-member Minister to become a member of either House of Parliament within six consecutive months; otherwise, the person ceases to be a Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the precise constitutional time limit and distinguish it from other parliamentary periods.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the ruling in S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001)?
o: A non-member cannot be repeatedly reappointed as Minister without getting elected.
Only a member of the Lok Sabha can be appointed as a Minister.
A non-member may be reappointed as Minister indefinitely without election.
A non-member cannot be appointed as Prime Minister under any circumstances.
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held that the constitutional provision for a non-member Minister cannot be used for repeated reappointments without the person securing election to the legislature.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the judicial limitation from the general six-month rule.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of Ministers:
1. Any person may be appointed as a Minister, subject to the constitutional six-month rule.
2. A non-member Minister must become a member of either House of Parliament within six months.
3. The six-month rule does not apply to a person appointed as Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the six-month rule applies to the Prime Minister as well.
accepted.tq: Find the exception that improperly excludes the Prime Minister from a general constitutional rule.

accepted.s: The constitutional basis of the collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers is
accepted.x: Article 75(3) provides that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional principle with the exact Article number.
accepted.sec: Council of Ministers - collective and individual responsibility

accepted.s: Which one of the following best represents individual responsibility of a Union Minister?
o: The Lok Sabha Speaker may dismiss a Minister for absence.
The Prime Minister may advise the removal of an individual Minister.
The entire Council must resign after defeat in a Rajya Sabha election.
The President may remove any Minister independently of the Prime Minister.
accepted.x: Individual ministerial responsibility is reflected in the Prime Minister's ability to have an individual Minister removed. The President formally removes the Minister on the Prime Minister's advice.
accepted.tq: Ask who would perform the personnel function in practice rather than relying only on formal wording.
accepted.sec: Council of Ministers - collective and individual responsibility

accepted.s: What is the constitutional consequence of the death or resignation of the Prime Minister?
o: The Rajya Sabha is automatically dissolved.
Only the Cabinet Secretariat is dissolved.
The Council of Ministers as a whole goes out of office.
The President assumes the office of Prime Minister permanently.
accepted.x: The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers; therefore, the death or resignation of the Prime Minister results in the Council of Ministers going out of office.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional consequence of the Prime Minister's departure.
accepted.sec: Council of Ministers - collective and individual responsibility

accepted.s: The oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers are administered by the
accepted.x: The President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers in accordance with the Third Schedule.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional authority associated with administering the oath.
accepted.sec: Council of Ministers - collective and individual responsibility

accepted.s: Under Article 74(1), the advice of the Council of Ministers becomes binding on the President after the President
o: secures approval from the Election Commission
refers the matter to the Supreme Court
obtains the consent of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.
accepted.tq: Focus on the one permitted reconsideration rather than an unlimited presidential discretion.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 74(2)
 b. Article 77(1)
 c. Article 77(2)
 d. Article 77(3)

List-II (Provision)
 i. Authentication of orders
 ii. Executive action expressed in the President's name
 iii. Advice not subject to inquiry by any court
 iv. Rules for convenient transaction and allocation of government business

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Article 74(2) concerns non-inquiry into ministerial advice; Article 77(1) concerns expression in the President's name; Article 77(2) concerns authentication; and Article 77(3) concerns transaction and allocation of business rules.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pairs and eliminate codes containing a misplaced constitutional subject.

accepted.s: The Rules of Government of India (Transaction of Business) and Allocation of Business are framed under the authority of
accepted.x: Article 77(3) enables the President to make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for allocation of such business among Ministers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the rule-making provision from the neighbouring provisions on advice and Prime Ministerial duties.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the Prime Minister under Article 78?
o: Furnishing information relating to administration when called for by the President
Submitting for the consideration of the Council any matter decided by an individual Minister when the President requires it
Communicating to the President decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals
Administering the oath of office and secrecy to all Union Ministers
accepted.x: Administering the oath to Union Ministers is a function of the President. The duties in options a, b and c are specified in Article 78.
accepted.tq: Find the one function belonging to the President rather than the Prime Minister.

accepted.s: If the President requires, the Prime Minister must place before the Council of Ministers for consideration a matter which has been decided by
accepted.x: Article 78(c) requires the Prime Minister to submit for the consideration of the Council any matter on which a Minister has taken a decision but which has not been considered by the Council, if the President so requires.
accepted.tq: Test the specific trigger and subject of the Prime Minister's Article 78(c) duty.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 77(1) deals with the expression of executive action in the President's name.
2. Article 77(2) deals with authentication of orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the President.
3. Article 78 deals with the Prime Minister's communication duties towards the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly identify the contents of Articles 77(1), 77(2) and 78.
accepted.tq: Verify each Article against its distinct constitutional function before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure of the Prime Minister?
o: The Prime Minister can be removed only by the Supreme Court.
The Prime Minister holds office for life unless removed by impeachment.
The Prime Minister continues in office while commanding the confidence of the Lok Sabha, subject to the President's pleasure in the constitutional sense.
The Prime Minister has a fixed tenure of five years irrespective of legislative support.
accepted.x: The Prime Minister has no fixed tenure and ordinarily continues while enjoying the confidence of the Lok Sabha. The Constitution formally states that Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure.
accepted.tq: Reject the fixed-term trap and connect tenure with legislative confidence.
accepted.sec: Prime Minister - appointment, qualifications, oath, real executive

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the President and the Prime Minister in the Indian parliamentary system?
o: The President is the de facto head of government and the Prime Minister is the de jure head of State.
The President is the de jure head of State and the Prime Minister is the de facto head of government.
The Prime Minister is the de jure head of State and the President is only a ceremonial officer of Parliament.
Both the President and the Prime Minister are de facto heads of government.
accepted.x: The President is the de jure head of the State, while the Prime Minister functions as the de facto head of government.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the paired constitutional and political roles rather than treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Prime Minister - appointment, qualifications, oath, real executive

accepted.s: During a National Emergency, the President of India
o: acquires unrestricted discretion to disregard the advice of the Council of Ministers
continues to be bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers
becomes the real executive in place of the Prime Minister
may dismiss the entire Council without following constitutional advice
accepted.x: A National Emergency does not confer discretionary power on the President to disregard the binding advice of the Council of Ministers. The parliamentary executive relationship continues.
accepted.tq: Guard against the emergency-powers trap by checking whether the constitutional advice requirement has been altered.

accepted.s: Article 75(2) was referred to in the acceptance of a Minister's resignation because that Article relates to
o: collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
the President's pleasure regarding the tenure of Ministers
the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information
accepted.x: Article 75(2) provides that Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which operates in practice on the advice of the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional clause to its operative subject instead of to a neighbouring Article.
accepted.sec: Prime Minister - appointment, qualifications, oath, real executive

accepted.s:
Arrange the following provisions in the order of their appearance in the Constitution:
A. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
B. Prime Minister's duties to communicate information to the President
C. All executive action expressed in the President's name
D. Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The provisions occur in the order Article 74(1), Article 75(3), Article 77(1) and Article 78: advice, collective responsibility, executive expression and Prime Ministerial duties.
accepted.tq: Use the Article numbers as the sequence: 74, 75, 77 and 78.
